memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "These are the laws you are to set before them:" - Exodus 21:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Just after the thunder and fire of Mount Sinai, God turns to something surprisingly ordinary — everyday rules about servants, injuries, and property. It can feel like a letdown after the Ten Commandments. But think about what this shows us of God's heart. He does not only care about grand moments of worship; He cares about how you treat the person working in your kitchen, how you handle a quarrel with your neighbour, how you drive on a crowded road. The same God who spoke the universe into being stoops down to give guidance for our daily muddles.

These laws were given to a particular nation at a particular time, so we do not follow them line by line today. Yet they reveal a God who wants fairness, dignity, and mercy woven into common life. Our faith is not meant to stay inside the four walls of a church building. It must show up in our homes, our shops, our offices. In Christ, the law finds its fullness (Matt 5:17), and love becomes the thread that ties every command together.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Where does my faith stop at the church door instead of entering my daily routine?
How does God's attention to small matters comfort me today?
Whom do I treat carelessly that God is asking me to honour?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You care about the ordinary corners of my life. Teach me to bring You into my everyday dealings and to treat others with the fairness and mercy You show me. Amen.
